why: Heavy Hearts is the Egyptian-themed pyramid club in Dogtown's Golden Pacific: neutral ground and business salon for the district's elite, with a bar, dance floor, VIP booths, doll booths and Mr. Hands' backroom suite. Vanilla only fills it through quest-community phases (heavy_hearts.questphase and ep1_community) that the clean slate never runs, so the club stands empty. This proposal re-activates the club's own ambient community entries - staff and VIP patrons, the main-floor crowd, the entrance queue and the Barghest security detail - plus the two quest sections those spawners live in and the four variant states that make the club read as open for business.

open_questions: The security entries use 'enemy_*_outside_sts' records with no spot map, so their stance is unknown: confirm on the tour that the bouncer and guards stand idle/non-hostile and do not open fire or aim, and that the netrunner stays at his post.

The #sts_ep1_06_com_civilians whole-community activation includes the two prosecutor/lawyer patrons and the doll-booth workers; check they are not frozen in a gig scene pose (prosecutor_002's initial phase is after_conversation).

The club's music/dancefloor lighting may come from #dancefloor_heavy_hearts (owned by dancefloors_ep1) or from monument_av_audio_prefabJNLTDZA's pyramid_music_default, neither of which is a toggle of this venue; confirm on the tour that the floor is lit and audible, otherwise add the missing prefab/toggle.

Mr. Hands: cast_and_hubs.json seats him on a #ws_mr_hands_default in the ne2 fixers prefab at world position ~6013/6115, while this venue also owns a #ws_mr_hands_default inside mr_hands_combat_zone_default_prefabPY55PSI at ~-1586/-2340 (his Heavy Hearts suite). If the owner wants him in the club, that is a cast-layer change, not a venue phase.
The wiki names Helen Wandoo (bartender) and Sarah Rossack (manager) but vanilla has no character records for them; they are covered only by generic waitress records.

Whether the terrace/rail and second-floor crowd entries picked here still read well once streamed; the crowd phases are single 'a' phase for all entries, so the exact room each entry lands in is only verified by the tour.

communities.why: The club's working staff and booth patrons in one vanilla whole-community activation: bartender (waitress/bar), fluff waitresses, technician, drug dealer and friend in the toilets, braindance and business guests in booths 3-4, doll-booth workers and VIP lounge lawyers. This is exactly what the ambient club phase switches on when no gig scene is running.

variant_toggles.why: Lights the club's heart sign; the ambient club phase switches it on for the open club and off for the gig's shut-down state.
Keeps the street-story interior trigger off, i.e. no gig scene inside the booth area; vanilla's ambient club phase sets exactly this.
Calm club ambience: the street story raises this parameter to 1 for its gunfight and sets it back to 0, so 0 is the open-for-business value.

The reception door is a baked mesh variant, not a device (playbook rule 14): the club's inner way in only exists with this toggle in the open state, which the ambient club phase and the post-gig cleanup both set.

proximity_wait.why: The club's main double entrance doors, on the only way in and streamed with the venue; vanilla's ambient club phase enables and powers them, so they are a device that reliably streams in before the crowd needs re-issuing (rule 8).
